title: Wideband Data Stations 303 Type

fixity.scan_notes: Key interface/product pages visually inspected during research; local checksum still pending.

redistribution_notes: Index/link until Bell/AT&T document redistribution status is established.

provenance.chain_notes: Earlier X303A interim/model-shop documents from 1964/1965 are named inside this reference and should receive separate records when recovered.

claims_extracted.claim: The 303 family included 303B at 19.2 kbit/s, 303C at 50 kbit/s, 303D at 230.4 kbit/s and 303E at 200 kbit/s classes.
claims_extracted.locator: general-description/product-family pages; visually verified in 1966 scan
claims_extracted.notes: Suffix-number options within each letter class remain to be cataloged.

claims_extracted.claim: A 50 kbit/s 303C-class service used group-band wideband facilities equivalent to the bandwidth of twelve voice circuits.
The high-speed business-machine interface used a 12-pin Burndy connector and was not simply an RS-232 serial interface.
claims_extracted.notes: Exact connector/pin assignment should be transcribed into artifact record in a later pass.

claims_extracted.claim: The manual documents a special government 50 kbit/s balanced-interface 303C application with 135-ohm balanced circuits and no clock interchange to the attached equipment.
claims_extracted.locator: Special Government Application — 50 Kilobits per second, Balanced Interface; visually verified
claims_extracted.notes: Do not infer this exact option was installed at every ARPANET site without site records.

claims_extracted.claim: The standardized 303 type was distinguished from earlier X303A interim/model-shop equipment documented in 1964 and supplemented in 1965.

notes: Product-family authority, not site-installation proof. Exact UCLA/SRI 1969 303 code remains unresolved.
